title: Add shared overload error-code enum + JSON schema for REST and OpenAI-compat endpoints
author: Brian Murphy
description:
Context: As part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (ENG-4821), we need deterministic, customer-actionable overload responses across both the standard REST endpoints and the OpenAI-compatible surface. Today we return a mix of 500/502/503 with inconsistent bodies and no stable machine-readable reason codes, which makes client retry behavior and support triage harder.

This PR introduces a shared overload error-code enum and a JSON Schema for Redwood overload errors, then wires both the REST and OpenAI-compat adapters to the same canonical payload + headers. The goal is consistency: same error codes, same Retry-After semantics, same request_id propagation, and an OpenAI-compat mapping that doesn’t break existing clients.

What’s in this PR: 1) New canonical error model: `OverloadErrorCode` enum (shared) and `OverloadErrorResponse` shape. 2) JSON Schema: `schemas/overload_error_response.schema.json` exported in the monorepo and referenced by the REST and OpenAI-compat handlers. 3) OpenAI-compat mapping: overload responses are still surfaced as `error: { message, type, code }` in OpenAI format, but `code` is now the Redwood overload code (string), and `type` is `redwood_overload_error` (new) while preserving the existing HTTP status. 4) Header contract: Always include `Retry-After` (seconds) when the error is retryable; always include `x-redwood-error-code`; preserve `x-request-id` / `x-redwood-request-id`.

Overload codes included (initial set): `overload_admission_control` (edge/gateway shed), `overload_circuit_open` (routing breaker open), `overload_queue_full` (runtime bounded queue hit), `overload_capacity_unavailable` (no eligible pools/regions), `overload_memory_pressure` (KV-cache/memory guardrail), `overload_streaming_disconnected` (server-initiated disconnect under overload; retryable depending on stage).

HTTP mapping (non-exhaustive): - 429 for `overload_admission_control` when we can deterministically shed early and the client can retry. - 503 for `overload_circuit_open` / `overload_capacity_unavailable` and cases where we are protecting control plane or capacity is temporarily unavailable. - 503 for runtime shed (`overload_queue_full`, `overload_memory_pressure`) with `Retry-After` to avoid immediate retry storms.

Notes / compatibility: - We do NOT change quota/rate limit error shapes here; this is overload-only. - We intentionally keep the OpenAI JSON envelope stable; only `error.code` becomes consistent and `error.type` is set to a Redwood-specific value. Clients that treat `error.code` as opaque should continue to work. - Schema is versioned via `$id` and a `schema_version` field in the canonical Redwood response (OpenAI-compat response does not include `schema_version` to avoid surprises).

Testing: - Unit tests for schema validation + round-trip serialization. - Contract tests for REST and OpenAI-compat handlers asserting status, body fields, and headers, including Retry-After presence for retryable codes. - Added a small fixture set for each overload code so future layers (routing/runtime) can reuse the same golden payloads.

Rollout: This is a library/contract PR; behavior is only visible when the admission control / breaker logic returns overload errors (ENG-4822/4824/4826). We’ll enable in one canary region/model first and monitor error mix and client retry behavior.

Refs: ADR-0147 (overload error taxonomy + HTTP mapping), SUP-3928/SUP-3961 (customer requests for clearer errors + Retry-After guidance).
commits: api/errors: introduce OverloadErrorCode enum + canonical payload model
schemas: add overload_error_response JSON schema + fixtures
openai-compat: map overload errors into OpenAI error envelope consistently
gateway: plumb x-redwood-error-code + Retry-After helpers (no behavior flip)
tests: add contract tests for REST/OpenAI overload error responses
review_conversation: Amara Diallo: Can we guarantee `Retry-After` is present for all retryable overload cases? Also prefer header name `x-redwood-error-code` (lowercase in code, but canonical header name should be documented).

Brian Murphy (author): Updated helper so retryable overload codes require Retry-After (seconds). Added tests that fail if missing. Header is now consistently emitted as `x-redwood-error-code` and documented in internal doc stub.

Jordan Lee: Please make sure code strings are stable (no env-specific suffixes) and align naming with ADR-0147. Also: we should avoid putting raw region/model in the error body to reduce accidental cardinality/PII concerns.

Brian Murphy (author): Renamed a couple codes to match ADR language (`overload_circuit_open`, `overload_capacity_unavailable`). Removed `region`/`model` fields from the body; those remain in logs/traces only.

Monica Patel: For SDKs, `error.code` should remain a string, but we need a clear place to hang machine-readable metadata. Can we add `retryable` and `retry_after_seconds` to the canonical Redwood body so SDKs don’t have to parse headers?

Brian Murphy (author): Added `retryable: boolean` and `retry_after_seconds?: number` to the canonical Redwood payload. OpenAI-compat stays header-first to minimize breaking changes; SDKs can read either.
Allison Grant: JSON schema looks good; please ensure we don’t introduce unbounded enums/labels. Also add `$id` and pin schema_version as a string to avoid accidental numeric parsing differences.
Brian Murphy (author): Added `$id`, made `schema_version` a string (`"2025-11-0"` for initial), and added a small note in schema about not adding new per-request fields without review.
Nikhil Sharma: Approved—this unblocks docs and support messaging. Please add a short note clarifying how this differs from rate limiting errors.
Brian Murphy (author): Added note to internal doc and description; rate limits remain separate.
release_notes: Internal: Introduces stable overload error codes + schema shared across REST and OpenAI-compat endpoints; SDKs can rely on `x-redwood-error-code` + `Retry-After` and canonical Redwood payload fields when applicable.
